sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk increases as the share of the credit limit in use rises.
Its effect is strongest at high utilization, rising steeply above about 0.785, while the number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver and risk increases with it.
The two interact strongly: the effect of utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies, so high utilization matters far more for applicants with delinquencies on file.
Annual income and length of credit history are the third and fourth most important drivers, and risk decreases as both rise.
Debt-to-income ratio adds a weak to moderate increase in risk, and recent credit inquiries have at most a weak effect.
The data do not settle whether the number of dependents or months at the current address matter for predictions, and applicant age hardly matters.
History length and recent inquiries reverse direction with each other: a longer history lowers risk only when inquiries are frequent.
Overall the model rests mainly on credit utilization and delinquency history, with the other features playing supporting roles.
